positions.name: KestrelwoodCalibrationVerification
positions.frame: What does verification against the June reference plates establish about the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration state — narrated confirmation, or a structured record entry?
positions.why: All three expressions report the identical calibration fact — instrument, 88.4 MHz value, and verification against the June reference plates — but perform it in two different registers: src-1 narrates the verification with expert, rational-persuasion authority ('We verified the calibration... it holds across the full observing band'), while src-2 and src-3 render the same fact as flat, informational labeled-field entries ('**Instrument**: ...', '**Calibration**: ...') with no persuasive framing. The set holds a tension between narrated confirmation and protocol-style record-keeping, both grounded in the same reference-plate verification and both converging on calm, unhedged, competence-oriented assertion.
